passage: Sunaina sat on the terrace in Bundi with a notebook, her phone charging by the water tank, and called the fifteen people who had stopped using her fitness app. She did not ask why they left. She asked, "What do you do now instead?" Sarika, who ran a women's morning walking group in the lane behind the temple, was the sixth call. "We have a group on a chat app with a trainer," said Sarika. "The trainer sends a voice note every morning and we reply with a photo." By the twelfth call the notebook had the same line repeating: a chat group, a trainer, a voice note. Only two people mentioned the app at all. Sunaina put the pen down. "It isn't that they don't want fitness," she told the water tank. "They want a person."

qa.q: How many people did Sunaina call?
qa.a: Sunaina called the fifteen people who had stopped using her app.

qa.q: What was Sunaina probably feeling when she put the pen down?
qa.a: Sunaina was probably feeling a sober realisation, perhaps disappointed but clearer, as she said people want a person.

qa.q: What could Sunaina build after these calls?
qa.a: Sunaina could make a simple tool that helps trainers run their chat groups, since that is what people already use.

qa.q: How might Sarika see the fitness app?
qa.a: Sarika may see the trainer's chat group as already doing the job, so the app was not needed.

grounding: Sunaina calls fifteen users who left her fitness app and learns they use a chat group with a trainer, which suggests a different product.

passage:
Vera had spent two years on the running app, and in Tallinn's long winter the numbers kept dropping. Instead of another redesign, she made a list of fifteen people who had stopped using it and called them one by one from her kitchen table.
She asked the same question each time: "What do you do now instead?" Emil, her co-founder, sat beside her with a notebook and made tally marks.
A retired teacher said she ran with a group now. A student said the same. A nurse said, "My trainer sends us a plan in a chat group every Monday, and we post our runs there." By the fifteenth call, Emil had eleven marks under "chat group with trainer".
Vera put the phone down. "They don't want an app to run alone with. They want a trainer and a group."

qa.q: How many marks did Emil have under "chat group with trainer"?
What was Vera feeling when she put the phone down?
qa.a: Vera was probably surprised and a little shaken, but also excited to see such a clear pattern.

qa.q: What could Vera and Emil test next?
qa.a: A simple trainer-led group with a few lapsed users, before building anything big.

qa.q: How does the nurse see what she needs to keep running?
qa.a: The nurse values the trainer's Monday plan and sharing runs with the group more than any app feature.

grounding: It shows a founder phoning fifteen lapsed users of a fitness app and learning most now use a chat group run by a trainer, which points to a different product.

passage:
In a glass cabin at the university incubator, Samir set his phone on speaker and ticked off names on a printed list: fifteen people who had stopped opening the home-workout app in the last two months. His co-founder, Tarun, held a stopwatch; they had promised each person no more than five minutes.
"I just want to understand what you do now instead," Samir said, again and again.
A software tester in Kochi: "My gym trainer made a chat group. She sends videos, we send photos." A mother of two: "My neighbour's yoga teacher runs a group; I do the morning session with them." By call fifteen, twelve people had described some kind of group led by a real trainer.
Tarun stopped the watch. "Nobody misses our videos. They miss a person checking on them."

qa.q: How many callers described a group led by a trainer?
What does Tarun's line about missing a person suggest he feels?
qa.a: Tarun seems struck and a bit humbled, recognising that the app's videos weren't what people valued.

qa.q: What product could Samir and Tarun explore?
qa.a: A tool that helps trainers run small groups and check on members, based on what twelve of fifteen callers described.

qa.q: What is it like for the mother of two in her neighbour's yoga group?
qa.a: She seems to enjoy the morning sessions with a real teacher and group, which suit her day better than app videos.

grounding: It shows founders calling fifteen lapsed fitness-app users to ask what they do instead and finding most follow trainer-led chat groups, suggesting a different product.
